entities.summary: Cao Xing (b. 200 CE) was a high-ranking civil servant of the Eastern Han dynasty, active in the Imperial capital of Luoyang. His administrative expertise played a significant role in maintaining order and stability during a period of internal conflict and external threats from nomadic groups. As a military leader, Cao Xing participated in several campaigns against the Wuhuan and Xiongnu tribes, ultimately contributing to the dynasty's survival. His leadership and strategic thinking earned him recognition among his peers and cemented his legacy as a prominent figure in Chinese history. The Eastern Han dynasty's emphasis on centralized administration and bureaucratic meritocracy, which Cao Xing exemplified, had a lasting impact on the development of Chinese governance and social hierarchy. The Cao Wei state, founded by Cao Xing's son Cao Pi, would go on to play a crucial role in shaping Chinese history during the Three Kingdoms period.
